title: The bedroom
description: Name the things in a bedroom, and say where each one is.
grammar: gender and articles, and saying where things are
grammarNote: Every noun in a room needs its article, and many of them are feminine.

explanation.summary: A bedroom is a small room with a fixed set of nouns in it. Once you know the words and the articles, you can describe any bedroom in two sentences.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: Most of these words end in -a, so most of them are feminine: la ventana, la puerta, la cortina. The ones that end in -o are masculine: el armario, el cajón, el póster. One word is shorter than the noun it comes from: la mesita is a smaller mesa, and the ending -ita makes it feminine.

sections.heading: Putting things where they go
sections.body: Use estar to say where a thing is, and a preposition to say where that is. Sobre la cama means on the bed, and en el armario means in the wardrobe. The bed is where most of these things end up, which makes it the most useful noun in the unit.

examples.es: la almohada está sobre la cama
examples.en: the pillow is on the bed

examples.es: la colcha está en la cama
examples.en: the quilt is on the bed

examples.es: el póster está en la pared
examples.en: the poster is on the wall

items.note: Feminine: la mesita. The ending -ita makes it smaller and feminine.
Masculine: el cajón. The plural is los cajones.

drills.meaning: the pillow is on the bed
the wardrobe is made of wood
